- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp moves; apply downward bias or dampen momentum.
- After a price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often fails to recognize it; align forecast with 10–15 day moving average of history.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); cap forecast at +2% above recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment history shows strong divergence from price trend (e.g., sentiment bullish but price falls), model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use 3-day rolling average of true values for smoothing.
